name: OR-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Cliff Bentz running with a 15-to-1 fundraising advantage
No polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
Prediction markets give Bentz about a 94% win chance
model.rationale: The baseline of R+15.9 is well supported by the district's R+14 lean, Bentz's incumbency, and his overwhelming cash advantage over Democrat Chris Beck, with no offsetting evidence. I keep the forecast essentially at the baseline, nudged slightly toward the fundamentals-based R+9.6 given the Democratic-leaning national environment.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Bentz under 55%, or major outside spending entering for Beck, would warrant a move toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern Oregon's 2nd District is solidly Republican, with a partisan lean of about fourteen points toward the GOP. Cliff Bentz, the incumbent, is running for reelection and holds a large financial edge, having raised roughly ten times as much as Democratic challenger Chris Beck and entering the fall with over $1.4 million on hand. There are no public polls of the race and no expert ratings, so the forecast relies on district fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, all of which point the same direction.

The main uncertainty is the national political environment, which leans Democratic this cycle and could narrow the margin somewhat, but a seat this red with a well-funded incumbent is very unlikely to flip. Bentz remains a heavy favorite.
